items.headline: FERC rejects Oklo's bid to rejoin PJM's interconnection queue
items.what_happened: FERC issued an order on September 24, 2026 under Docket EL26-101 denying Oklo's complaint that had sought to force PJM to reinstate a 750 MW hybrid project — 150 MW of advanced nuclear generation plus 300 MW of fuel cells and 300 MW of gas-fired generation, near Richmond, Virginia — into PJM's current interconnection study cycle. PJM had withdrawn the project in August after citing application defects it said Oklo never fixed.
items.why_it_matters: The order confirms FERC will hold co-located nuclear-plus-generation projects to ordinary interconnection-queue discipline, adding at least 18 months of delay risk for any microreactor developer planning a hybrid or behind-the-meter deployment on PJM's grid.
items.binding_note: A final FERC order denying the complaint; Oklo can refile in PJM's next study cycle or use the Expedited Interconnection Track, open through December 31, 2027.

sources.label: Utility Dive — FERC rejects Oklo complaint seeking to reinstate project to PJM's interconnection study cycle (2026)
sources.quote: failed to demonstrate PJM violated its tariff

items.headline: TRISO-X finishes vertical construction on its Oak Ridge fuel plant
items.what_happened: TRISO-X, X-energy's fuel subsidiary, announced on September 24, 2026 that it completed vertical construction of the 214,000-square-foot TX-1 fuel fabrication facility in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, completing the building's primary structure and clearing the way for interior build-out and fuel-fabrication equipment installation.
items.why_it_matters: TX-1 is sized to produce about 700,000 TRISO-X pebbles a year, enough for up to 11 Xe-100-class reactors, so its construction pace is a trackable leading indicator of when a second qualified TRISO fuel source becomes available to microreactor buyers.

sources.label: GlobeNewswire — TRISO-X Completes Vertical Construction of TX-1 Fuel Fabrication Facility (2026)
sources.quote: TX-1 is expected to produce approximately 700,000 TRISO-X fuel pebbles annually

items.headline: Samsung C&T signs binding term sheet to invest $100M in Kairos
items.what_happened: Kairos Power and Samsung C&T announced a binding term sheet on September 21, 2026 under which Samsung C&T will provide up to $100 million — roughly $70 million as a direct equity stake and the rest as in-kind engineering services — toward the 50 MWe Hermes 2 demonstration plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, and will join Kairos's EPC team.
items.why_it_matters: Pairing a strategic investor's cash with its own in-kind EPC labor, layered under a corporate offtake letter (Google), is a financing template a microreactor vendor could copy to bridge the gap between a signed offtake and the capital needed to build a first-of-a-kind unit.
items.binding_note: A signed, binding term sheet; the investment itself is still subject to regulatory approvals and definitive agreements.

sources.label: Kairos Power — Kairos Power and Samsung C&T Agree to Pursue Strategic Investment and Collaboration for KP-FHR Deployment (2026)
sources.quote: up to $100 million through a combination of direct investment and in-kind engineering services

items.headline: EIB makes its first-ever SMR loan, to Finland's Steady Energy
items.what_happened: The European Investment Bank announced on September 15, 2026 a senior unsecured convertible loan of up to EUR40 million (about $46 million) to Finnish developer Steady Energy, funding R&D, testing and licensing of its 50 MWt LDR-50 district-heating reactor through 2028.
items.why_it_matters: It is the EIB's first-ever SMR financing after the bank generally avoided new nuclear — a public development-bank debt structure that a microreactor developer targeting district heat or industrial steam, not just electricity, can point to when courting a multilateral lender.

sources.label: World Nuclear News — First SMR funding agreed by European Investment Bank (2026)

items.headline: NuCube-Launch Two SPAC merger's S-4 goes public with the SEC
items.what_happened: Launch Two Acquisition Corp (Nasdaq: LPBB) publicly filed a Form S-4 registration statement with the SEC on September 11, 2026 for its proposed business combination with microreactor developer NuCube Energy, first agreed under a business combination agreement dated June 25, 2026. Closing still requires shareholder votes at both companies.
items.why_it_matters: A public S-4 is the fullest paper trail so far of a microreactor developer's capitalization and governance terms — real diligence material next to peers who have only announced funding rounds in press releases.
items.binding_note: The S-4 filing itself is an executed SEC filing; the merger has not closed and still needs shareholder approval.

items.headline: Navy picks Crane, Indiana for its first shore-based microreactor
items.what_happened: The Department of War announced on September 9, 2026 the planned installation of Indiana's first advanced nuclear Micro Modular Reactor at Naval Weapons Station Crane, executed jointly through the Army's Janus Program and Navy energy offices, with installation targeted no later than September 2028. No commercial reactor vendor was named.
items.why_it_matters: Crane is the first Navy site in the Janus pipeline, showing the Army-run microreactor program is expanding beyond the Army — a bigger federal buyer base for 1-20 MW reactors, though no vendor or contract value is attached yet.
items.binding_note: A site-selection and planning announcement; no vendor, reactor design or contract value has been disclosed.

sources.quote: the planned installation of the State of Indiana's first advanced nuclear Micro Modular Reactor (MMR) at Naval Weapons Station (NWS) Crane

items.headline: eVinci hits criticality at full operating temperature in Nevada
items.what_happened: Westinghouse's eVinci test unit reached criticality at 663°C on September 3, 2026 at the National Critical Experiments Research Center in Nevada, with a peak core temperature of 1,011°C, in a joint test run with Los Alamos and Idaho National Laboratories, the Nevada National Security Site and the DOE/NRC criticality-safety collaboration.
items.why_it_matters: This is a harder milestone than eVinci's zero-power criticality three weeks earlier: proving the core goes critical near its real operating temperature generates the performance data microreactor buyers will eventually see cited in eVinci's NRC license application.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Energy — Westinghouse eVinci Microreactor Achieves Criticality Milestone (2026)
sources.quote: a peak core temperature of 1,011 degrees Celsius, a record-high temperature

items.headline: Radiant's Kaleidos microreactor departs for INL's DOME test bed
items.what_happened: Radiant shipped a full-scale Kaleidos test unit from its El Segundo, California factory on August 12, 2026, bound for Idaho National Laboratory's DOME facility, where it will run a five-phase test campaign from zero-power criticality through a targeted 150-hour full-power run.
items.why_it_matters: Kaleidos is the first DOE-selected DOME design to actually ship hardware, so its transport and pending test timeline is the concrete benchmark other DOME-track microreactor vendors will be measured against.
items.binding_note: An achieved shipment milestone; zero-power criticality and later test phases were not yet confirmed as of this capture date.

sources.label: World Nuclear News — Kaleidos microreactor begins journey to Idaho (2026)
sources.quote: from zero-power criticality, through to generating full heat and power

items.headline: DOE approves nuclear safety design agreement for Deep Fission
items.what_happened: The U.S. Department of Energy approved a Nuclear Safety Design Agreement for Deep Fission's Gravity reactor on August 6, 2026, covering its pilot unit at the Great Plains Industrial Park in Parsons, Kansas, and setting the safety-analysis approach for its Reactor Pilot Program demonstration.
items.why_it_matters: Deep Fission's borehole-sited design (a mile underground rather than a factory-built surface module) is a different site-prep model than most 1-20 MW peers, so this NSDA is a second data point on how flexible DOE's safety-design framework is across very different reactor geometries.

sources.label: Deep Fission, Inc. — Department of Energy Approves Nuclear Safety Design Agreement for Deep Fission's Gravity Reactor (2026)
sources.quote: establishes the safety framework that will guide the reactor's continued development

items.headline: NRC proposes higher radiation limits for microreactor transport
items.what_happened: The NRC put out a proposed rule (published in the Federal Register on July 27, 2026, Docket NRC-2025-1667) that would let certain Type B transport packages carrying irradiated microreactors qualify for a higher radiation limit of 50 mrem/h at 2 meters, up from the current 10 mrem/h, under exclusive-use controls. The public comment period closed August 26, 2026.
items.why_it_matters: Microreactors are sold on being truckable and field-swappable, so how the NRC certifies packages for shipping an irradiated core, not just fresh fuel, is a direct cost and schedule input for any 1-20 MW vendor planning to move a spent or exchanged core off-site.
items.binding_note: A proposed rule out for public comment, not yet finalized.

items.headline: FedDev Ontario awards CSMC $4.5M for Arctic microreactor design
items.what_happened: The Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario awarded Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation $4.5 million on July 23, 2026 to fund detailed design and a fuelled demonstration of its micro-nuclear reactor system for deployment in Canada's Arctic.
items.why_it_matters: A second, separate Canadian federal funding stream — regional economic-development money, not defence procurement — now backs a microreactor developer directly, a route smaller vendors without a defence contract can pursue alongside DND's own program.

sources.label: Newswire.ca (Cision) — Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation awarded $4.5 million through the Government of Canada to accelerate micro-nuclear technology for Canada's Arctic (2026)

items.headline: Canada's defence department commits $40M to Arctic microreactor study
items.what_happened: Canada's Minister of National Defence, Tim Hodgson, announced on April 29, 2026 that the department would spend $40 million in the 2026-27 fiscal year to study whether microreactors can supply heat and electricity to remote northern military facilities, part of a push toward a 2028 demonstration reactor.
items.why_it_matters: A defence department funding its own feasibility study, rather than just responding to a vendor's pitch, is a more durable government-buyer signal than the MOUs that otherwise dominate this market's early demand side.
items.binding_note: Reported as a funded departmental commitment for the current fiscal year rather than a completed procurement; no vendor or site is yet named.

sources.label: The Globe and Mail — Ottawa commits millions to study micro nuclear reactors for Northern military bases (2026)
sources.quote: spend $40-million this year to study the feasibility of using microreactors to provide heat and electricity to military facilities in remote and northern areas

items.headline: Yukon and Ontario sign pact to explore small modular reactors
items.what_happened: Yukon's Minister of Energy, Mines and Resources Ted Laking and Ontario's Minister of Energy and Mines Stephen Lecce signed a partnership agreement on April 22, 2026 for Yukon Energy and Ontario Power Generation to share technical, regulatory and financing groundwork on small modular reactors and microreactors for Yukon's grid.
items.why_it_matters: The pact explicitly reaches to microreactors sited off the electricity grid, making Yukon the first Canadian territory to formally scope microreactors for isolated, non-military communities rather than only defence bases, though it commits no money, timeline or site.
items.binding_note: A cooperation framework only; it does not commit Yukon to building any reactor or set a timeline.

items.headline: NANO Nuclear and Ameresco sign non-binding microreactor MOU
items.what_happened: NANO Nuclear Energy and Ameresco announced a memorandum of understanding on January 12, 2026 to jointly evaluate siting, licensing, construction and decommissioning of NANO's KRONOS MMR, ZEUS and LOKI microreactor designs on U.S. federal and commercial sites, with Ameresco positioned to lead future EPC work.
items.why_it_matters: It pairs a microreactor vendor with an established federal EPC/ESCO contractor before any site is named, a template other vendors without in-house construction capability may need, but it commits neither party to build anything.
items.binding_note: Explicitly a non-binding statement of intention; no site, schedule or price has been set.
